Immediate actions we are initiating now (T-0):
- Toggle cross-region routing priority to prefer US-WEST-2 for Helios production traffic. This will steer ~85% of traffic off AZ1 while preserving affinity for sticky sessions.
- Initiate a graceful drain of AZ1 serving nodes for Helios' namespace (connections allowed to finish, no new long-running sessions).
- Disable aggressive autoscaling for AZ1 to avoid spin-up amplification while traffic shifts.
- Collect and upload routing traces + kernel metrics to the incident folder.

Subject: Re: AZ1: major latency spike + 5xx surge — urgent

Quick tech notes from runtime side:
- Kernel-level backlog observed on the kv-cache path: lookups falling back to main memory on ~12% of requests which multiplied latency on long tails. Suspected cause: network-missed cache replications under partial partition.
- Mitigation applied: reduced KV replication window and forced local-hot-cache mode for affected az1 shards — this reduces cross-AZ chatter at the cost of slightly elevated cold misses.
- We're keeping AZ1 serving pool readable but preventing new long sessions; this prevents more cache divergence.

I'll continue to monitor error-rate delta and rollback the local-hot-cache if recovery is visible and stable for 30 mins.

Rishi
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
